projects.title: idea.quest
projects.pitch: A published 3D workshop whose project status can be edited in the Vault and automatically published after validation.
projects.nextMove: Step 5: decide whether to stop at the accepted status-only automatic-publish route or authorize one bounded next change. Website code/design publishing is outside this monitor.

updates.text: Vihaan confirmed the post-login status update and directed continuation. Step 4 human check accepted for the status-only route (4/5); Step 5 keep/revise/stop remains open.

Built and live-tested a scoped status-only monitor. A project-note next-step edit automatically reached Vercel after tests and hash checks; public JSON showed 3/5 and the new next step while visual assets stayed unchanged. Human acceptance and reboot persistence remain open.

Vihaan chose status only for the first automatic-publish test. Project records and approved gate status are candidate inputs; website design/code and private Vault content are excluded. No monitor or deployment has been built.

Vihaan selected automatic publishing after each validated edit, not preview-and-approval publishing. A feasibility note recommends a scoped local monitor as the first test; no automation or deployment has been built or approved.

Vihaan clarified that he wants to direct edits from either Obsidian Claudian or the ChatGPT desktop app. This is a workflow requirement, not authorization for a specific sync architecture or public write access.
Vihaan answered no to accepting the public read-only/manual-republish boundary. Step 4 remains active; the desired replacement behavior has not yet been specified or built.

Vihaan reported that tapping and dragging the published workshop on his actual phone are working fine. Device/browser details and measured frame rate were not reported. This is Step 4 evidence, not approval of the whole Human check gate.

After the ESF test audit, Vihaan explicitly accepted the current published idea.quest build as the Step 3 prototype. The Prototype gate is 3/5; Human check is active. This acceptance does not assert real-phone performance or approve Steps 4 or 5.

Improved the separate local 3D room with original wood, lighting, window, lantern, cat expressions, jar seals/glow, and game-menu styling. Build/tests and 390px emulated layout check passed. It remains visibly below commercial game art quality; Step 3 and public replacement are unapproved.

At user direction, integrated the working context-chat into the existing 2D ASCII board before returning to the separate 3D makeover. Local AI prompts work; public mirror offers a labelled registry-only status guide, not hosted AI chat. No gate changed.
User opened the local context-chat and reported that it works but looks generic. Functional behavior is a candidate; visual direction remains open. No gate or public deployment changed.

User approved a bounded local read-only context-chat spike. The separate site now shows recorded status and sources; an actual Codex prompt correctly reported idea.quest 2/5 and the paused unapproved 3D Step 3. Await user review; no gate or public deployment changed.

User clarified that context and understanding matter more than sharing the exact Claudian session. Proposed a local read-only chat test with explicit vault context; no chat build, remote access, or gate approved.

Paused 3D Step 3 review to explore a Codex chat/status side feature. Feasibility note compares status-only, local chat, and owner-only remote bridge. Public site is unchanged; no new gate or chat route approved.

Built an isolated read-only Three.js feasibility slice. The real registry now yields 2/2/5; a clearly labelled in-memory demo shows 0/2/5. Local browser and automated checks passed; visual approval remains pending.
User chose and approved Route C, a Three.js 3D room, with the existing public ASCII site kept live. Step 3 begins as an isolated small test; no public redesign deployment.
User provisionally approved Step 1's Midnight Workshop goal and three-jar scope. Only the Goal gate advanced; route and build remain pending.
Potion-room redesign drafted for review: one table, an original cat witch, and three data-driven jars. Goal gate remains unapproved; existing project records are preserved.
The ASCII cat now blinks, flicks its tail, and winks on hover; it also appears in the compact layout and respects reduced motion.
Added restrained icon motion, press/hover feedback, and approval-only checkpoint animation; reduced-motion preference disables them.
An owner-private read-only web mirror was deployed. It checks the public vault repo after sync; online edits are not enabled.
A working local prototype was built. No workflow gate is marked approved just because it runs.
